Redmond project planning

Plan adus around the actual property.

A Redmond mailing address alone does not establish city jurisdiction. Check the parcel before planning an addition or backyard building, then locate easements, trees, drainage paths, and the existing service connections on the same site plan.

Compare an internal conversion, attached unit, and detached unit before selecting a design. The site, utility routes, independent access, and retained household use determine which option deserves detailed planning.

  • Parcel eligibility and the applicable local development requirements
  • Water, wastewater, power, heating, and utility connection routes
  • Independent entry, privacy, light, and compact storage
  • Building placement, delivery access, and construction staging

Construction readiness

Coordinate the site, weather protection, and materials.

Before refreshing an exterior, follow the route of water from roof edges to downspouts and away from the foundation. Repair wet substrates and poorly integrated flashings before covering them with new finishes.

For an occupied Redmond home, decide which entrance remains available, where materials can be staged, and how deliveries avoid the household's daily arrival and departure times. A phased plan should preserve a usable bathroom where the scope allows it.

Local review

Permitting and scope in Redmond

For Redmond, begin with City of Redmond. Verify the property's jurisdiction and the scope before using a permit application or planning an inspection.

Confirm the current ADU rules and parcel conditions with the reviewing agency. Do not assume a standard size, exemption, parking rule, or approval timeline applies to every address. Utility and site approvals may be separate from building review.

Investment and timing

What shapes a Redmond adus estimate?

Separate feasibility and design, site preparation, service connections, structure, finishes, and permit-related costs. A small dwelling can have significant utility and access work that floor area does not reveal.

The first assessment identifies existing conditions, proposed changes, material decisions, access, and the review pathway. RT develops project-specific recommendations rather than assigning a price or completion date from a photo alone.

Your first conversation

Bring the information that changes the plan.

Share the intended use, whether the unit is attached or detached, known utility arrangements, parcel information, and privacy priorities.

Include the Redmond property address or ZIP code, your preferred timing, and the investment range you are considering. Plans and surveys are helpful when available, but you can start the conversation without them.

What the work includes

A coordinated adus scope

Discovery and site assessment

We clarify goals, review existing conditions, identify constraints, and determine what needs deeper investigation before a scope is written.

Design and pre-construction

Layout, materials, trade requirements, permits, allowances, schedule factors, and decision deadlines are coordinated into one buildable plan.

Construction and completion

The work is sequenced, protected, inspected, communicated, and closed out with a final walkthrough and documented completion items.

  • Site, setback, access, and feasibility review
  • Attached, detached, and conversion design
  • Utility, drainage, energy, and structural coordination
  • Permitting and jurisdiction-specific documentation
  • Compact kitchens, bathrooms, storage, daylight, and privacy

Official local resources

Check the requirements for your property.

Start with City of Redmond. Requirements depend on the parcel and scope; confirm the current pathway before relying on a permit assumption.

Redmond planning and permit resources

Questions homeowners ask

Redmond adus FAQs

Does RT offer adus in Redmond?

Yes. RT Signature Homes evaluates adus projects in Redmond from its Redmond base. Availability and the next step depend on the address, scope, timing, and current capacity.

Which agency should we check for a Redmond project?

For Redmond, begin with City of Redmond. Verify the property's jurisdiction and the scope before using a permit application or planning an inspection. Municipal review, trade permits, utilities, and private association approvals can involve different responsibilities. The official local resource linked on this page is the starting point, not a property-specific approval.

What is the first step for an ADU?

Confirm the property, jurisdiction, access, utilities, setbacks, and intended use before investing in a detailed design.

Can an existing garage become an ADU?

Sometimes. Foundation, ceiling height, structure, moisture, insulation, egress, utilities, parking rules, and code compliance must be evaluated.

Are the projects shown on this page located in this community?

Each project is labeled with its actual location. Related work elsewhere illustrates RT's construction and finish coordination; it is not presented as a project at your address or in your community.
